title: Incorporate regional outage postmortem actions into PRD: prioritized routing & deterministic fallbacks
creator: Rohan Patel
description: Following the March regional outage (us-west-2) postmortem, several operational and product-level actions were recommended. This ticket formalizes which postmortem items must be translated into formal PRD requirements and acceptance criteria so engineering and SRE have clear contracts for implementation, testing, and rollout. The focus areas are prioritized routing policies, deterministic fallback behavior when a region is degraded, and observable rollout guards to prevent cascades during recovery.
problem_statement: A partial regional outage exposed gaps between our incident runbook actions and what the serving runtime will automatically do: requests were routed suboptimally, fallbacks produced inconsistent model variants, and there were insufficient acceptance tests to validate graceful degradation semantics. This PRD update should close those gaps and provide measurable SLO/QA gates.
goals: Translate specific postmortem action items into unambiguous PRD requirements
Define deterministic fallback policies and ordering for model/region/instance variants
Add acceptance tests and canary checks to validate routing/fallback behavior
Specify observability signals and thresholds that gate automated rollouts
Minimize customer visible errors during partial region degradation
scope_changes: Add a new requirements section to runtime PRD describing prioritized routing rules (region > cost-tier > model-variant)
Introduce deterministic fallback matrix (compatible model variants + capacity tiers) to PRD; implementation details left to ENG
Require explicit acceptance tests for simulated region latency and partial outage scenarios (integration + chaos tests)
Exclude deeper kernel optimization work; those will be tracked separately as ENG follow-ups
Include a rollout guard requirement in Console: per-route SLO breakpoints and automatic rollback on breach
acceptance_criteria: Routing: Given a simulated region degradation, request routing follows priority order and routes only to allowed regions/tiers as defined in the PRD
Fallbacks: When the primary model/variant is unavailable, system selects the next compatible variant deterministically and documents the selection rationale
Tests: Integration test harness reproduces the March outage conditions and validates no more than X% increased error rate (threshold specified by SRE) during failover
Observability: Console shows per-route SLO and an automated alert that triggers the rollback policy when thresholds exceeded
Runbook: Postmortem-driven playbook entries are linked from the PRD and include the exact sequence of actions and owner roles
decisions: Prioritized routing will be policy-driven with explicit ordering (region, capacity-tier, variant) rather than probabilistic weighted routing
Deterministic fallback matrix will be the single source of truth; runtime must implement selection logic matching the matrix
Acceptance tests will be required before granting canary expansion beyond 5% traffic during rollout
Console SLO gates will be the primary automation trigger for rollback; manual override allowed with documented justification
follow_up_tasks: Create PRD section draft and circulate to ENG/SRE/Design by 2025-03-20
Work with ENG to enumerate exact compatibility matrix for commonly used models by 2025-03-28
Define integration test scenarios and add to CI (owner: ENG)
Add Console dashboard mockups and SLO gate behaviors (owner: Design + Product)
metrics: error-rate increase during simulated outage (target: < 0.5% absolute increase)
successful fallback selection rate (target: 100% deterministic selection)
test_plan: Unit tests for fallback selection logic
Integration tests using the chaos harness to simulate region latency and instance terminations
End-to-end canary that verifies SLO gates and rollback behavior before global rollout
Load tests across model variants to validate no regression in token throughput under fallback
risks: Over-constraining fallback rules could cause higher latency if nearby regions are blocked
Incomplete compatibility matrix may result in silent quality regressions when falling back to lower-capacity variants
Tight SLO gates could cause frequent rollbacks during noisy neighbor events unless thresholds tuned
roll_out_plan: Phase 1: Internal canary (5% traffic) with synthetic outage tests run continuously
Phase 2: Region-limited rollout to non-critical routes with increased observability
Phase 3: Global rollout after 2 weeks of stable canary metrics and post-rollout review
Rollback: automatic rollback triggered by Console SLO gate or manual rollback with documented reason
notes: This PRD update is intentionally implementation-agnostic: it specifies the observable behavior and acceptance tests rather than internal APIs
SRE to propose SLO thresholds; Product will bake thresholds into PRD once SRE provides historical baselines
We will re-evaluate requirements after initial rollout and may follow with a second PRD focusing on cost-aware routing
